body:
We make Kiron, so weigh this accordingly. Everything here about Runna comes from its App Store listing, its help and press pages, recent App Store reviews and the independent running site the5krunner, checked November 15, 2026. Everything about Kiron describes version 1.2.

Runna's strength sessions are built to make you a sturdier runner, and they do that job. If you want your squat or bench to keep going up, they're thin. Here's how Kiron (that's us) plans a week of lifting and running, and when Runna is still the right app.

Runna or Kiron? The quick answer

  • Choose Kiron if lifting matters as much as running: one plan for both, with a full lifting program that adds weight as you get stronger, for {{kiron:price-annual}} against Runna's $119.99. It doesn't record runs or show pace.
  • Use both if you lift seriously and you're chasing a race time: Runna for the runs, Kiron for the lifting, at $119.99 plus {{kiron:price-annual}}.
  • Stay with Runna alone if a race is the goal and one or two strength sessions a week is all the lifting you want. That's what they're built for.

Bottom line: Runna is a running coach with strength on the side; Kiron is a training plan where lifting and running share the week. If you're a lifter who runs, we think Kiron fits better, for less than half the price.

What Kiron is

Kiron is a workout app for {{kiron:cell-platforms}} that runs a training program for you, lifting and cardio together. Start in one of three ways:

  • Pick one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs by goal: lifting, running or both.
  • Answer a few questions and Kiron builds one.
  • Bring your own plan. Paste one from a coach or ChatGPT, or snap a photo, and Kiron turns it into a program on your calendar, phases and all.

Then there's little to think about:

  • Your next workout is ready when you open the app, whether you train on set days or whenever you make it to the gym. On set days, Kiron can move a missed session forward for you.
  • Your weights go up as you get stronger, and Kiron tells you why: "You hit every set, so we added 5 lb."
  • First-time weights are suggested with a short note saying why. After a set, Kiron asks how it felt and adjusts the rest.
  • Variety that keeps your main lifts, plus saved gyms for travel: switch to a hotel gym and Kiron swaps in exercises that fit.
  • Runs, rides, swims and rows on the same calendar, with plans from a first 5K to a marathon or a sprint triathlon.
  • Recovery that counts your runs, including ones your watch or running app saves to Apple Health or Health Connect. When today's lifting leans on tired legs, Kiron says why and offers an easier session.
  • Less than half Runna's yearly price: {{kiron:price-annual}}, against $119.99.

What Runna's strength sessions are for

Runna, which Strava bought in 2025, is a running coach in an app: it builds a plan around your race, sets your paces from your ability and recent race times, and suggests new ones as you train. Strength is an add-on, built to serve the running.

You add it under Plan, then Manage Plan, then Strength. Pick Running Focus, which works legs and core with minimal upper body, or All-Round Strength, which balances the two. Sessions run 30, 45 or 60 minutes, up to four a week, fitted to the equipment you tick. Runna suggests one a week to hold strength during heavy running, and up to three in the off-season.

Its help pages spell out the limits. You can't create your own strength workouts or swap an exercise in the app, though you can skip one. Runna keeps the weights you log but doesn't describe adding weight for you. Strength sessions stay on your phone, not your watch. And according to the5krunner, they're part of the paid subscription.

Reviewers are split. Of 500 recent US App Store reviews (January to November 2026), 41 mention strength, lifting, weights or the gym. Of those about the sessions, at least 14 praise them and 10 criticize them, mostly as too light, not editable or wrong for their equipment. One called the lifts "basically just a 45 minute warmup" (an App Store reviewer, June 2026). Both can be true: they're support work for running.

You've outgrown them if you want a lift to climb on a schedule, want your own exercises, lift more than four times a week or longer than an hour, or already follow a program from a coach, a book or ChatGPT.

Lifting and running in one Kiron plan

Kiron's Run + Lift program is the simplest version: two full-body barbell days and two runs a week, with no end date. Its suggested week:

  • Monday: squat, bench press and barbell row, then dumbbell step-ups.
  • Wednesday: a 35-minute easy run, at a pace where you can talk.
  • Thursday: one heavy set of deadlifts, then overhead press, chin-ups and dumbbell Romanian deadlifts.
  • Sunday: a long run of 5 miles, adding half a mile every other week.

Thursday's deadlift is a single heavy set so your legs recover before Sunday, and Wednesday's run stays easy after Monday's squats. Our guide to running and lifting in the same week explains the spacing.

Training for a race? Kiron's running plans go from Beginner 5K (9 weeks) to Marathon (16 weeks), and the longer ones ease off before race day. Start one next to a lifting program, such as the Beginner 5×5 in our post on StrongLifts alternatives, and both share one calendar. For a bigger week, the 7-Day Longevity Protocol puts three lifting days beside a tempo run, air-bike sprints and a long easy run, for 16 weeks.

How runs work in Kiron. Each run has a time or distance target and an effort cue, like "comfortably hard" for a tempo run. Kiron doesn't record runs or show pace: run with your watch or phone app, then type in the time and distance. On a busy day you can shorten or lengthen a run.

Runna for the runs, Kiron for the lifting

Chasing a race time? Keep Runna for what it does well and let Kiron run the lifting:

  1. In Runna, set your runs per week, running days and long-run day under Plan, then Manage Plan, then Running Schedule, and skip its strength setup.
  2. In Kiron, start a lifting program such as Upper / Lower Strength, four days a week. In Whenever I train mode, the next lifting session waits for whichever day Runna leaves free. Keep 24 to 36 hours between your heaviest leg day and your fastest run.
  3. Connect them through Health. If your Runna or watch runs land in Apple Health or Health Connect, Kiron's recovery map counts them next to your lifting. Check that they do first.

Runna is also sold in a Strava + Runna bundle for $149.99 a year, annual only, through Strava. Runna's free week and trial length come from the5krunner (October 2026). Prices vary by country and offer.

On the yearly plans, Kiron costs less than half what Runna does. Paying monthly, it's {{kiron:price-monthly}}, against Runna's $19.99.

Who should stay with Runna

  • A race time is the goal. Runna sets your paces and adjusts them as you train; Kiron gives time or distance targets and shows no pace.
  • You want your runs recorded. Runna records them on your phone, Apple Watch, Garmin or COROS watch. Kiron doesn't record runs and has no Watch app.
  • Strength is support work for you. One or two sessions a week, fitted to your equipment, come with the subscription.
  • You'd use the community: the Runna club, its events, and live yoga and pilates classes. Kiron has no social feed.
  • You want a longer free look. Runna's first week of any plan is free, and signing up directly comes with a 7-day trial. Kiron has {{kiron:trial}}, but no free week.
  • You value a track record. Runna has about 36,000 ratings on the US App Store, averaging 4.8, and an Editors' Choice badge. Kiron is new and still small.

What lifters ask about Runna

Does Runna have strength training?

Yes: pre-built Running Focus or All-Round Strength sessions of 30 to 60 minutes, up to four a week, fitted to your equipment. You can't create your own or swap exercises in the app.

How much is Runna?

On the US App Store, Runna Premium is $19.99 a month or $119.99 a year, and the Strava + Runna bundle is $149.99 a year. Without paying, you get week 1 of any plan plus run recording, according to the5krunner.

Is Runna worth it if I mostly lift?

If you run two or three times a week without a race time in mind, you may not need a running coach: easy runs plus one longer run cover it, and Kiron's Run + Lift puts exactly that beside your lifting. Chasing a race time? Runna's pace coaching is worth paying for.

Can I use Runna with a lifting app?

Yes; the setup is above. Our guide to workout apps for following a program covers other lifting apps too.

Is there a free way to run and lift?

Partly. Runna's free tier covers week 1 of any plan and recording your runs. For lifting, Hevy's free plan logs unlimited workouts with up to 4 saved routines (see Hevy vs Kiron), and Boostcamp offers most of its coach-made programs free. {{kiron:free-tier-sentence}}

If you lift first and run second, try Kiron's Run + Lift, or start a race plan next to the lifting program you already follow. {{kiron:cta-sentence}} Get Kiron.

If pace coaching for a race is what you're after, Runna is the right tool, and its first week is free.
